recipes.title: The Best Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies Recipe by Tasty
recipes.description: There are a few crucial steps to baking the chewiest, tastiest chocolate chip cookies. First, skip using chips and opt for chunks. Second, instead of using just one type of chocolate (like semisweet), use a mix of semisweet, milk, and dark chocolate. Third, take the time to allow the cookie dough to rest overnight in the refrigerator. Yes, we know it's a pain, but doing so will yield a cookie with a more complex flavor and delicious toffee notes. Lastly, use an ice cream scoop to portion the cookie dough onto the baking sheet. This will produce even-sized cookies every single time. Follow these simple steps, and you'll be rewarded with a cookie that's crisp and chewy on the outside and gooey on the inside!
ingredients: 4 oz milk or semi-sweet chocolate chunks
4 oz dark chocolate chunk, or your preference
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together the sugars, salt, and butter until a paste forms with no lumps.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla, beating until light ribbons fall off the whisk and remain for a short while before falling back into the mixture.
Sift in the flour and baking soda, then fold the mixture with a spatula (Be careful not to overmix, which would cause the gluten in the flour to toughen resulting in cakier cookies).

Fold in the chocolate chunks, then chill the dough for at least 30 minutes. For a more intense toffee-like flavor and deeper color, chill the dough overnight. The longer the dough rests, the more complex its flavor will be.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Scoop the dough with an ice-cream scoop onto a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, leaving at least 4 inches (10 cm) of space between cookies and 2 inches (5 cm)  of space from the edges of the pan so that the cookies can spread evenly.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until the edges have started to barely brown.
Cool completely before serving.
Enjoy!

recipes.title: Easy sardine butter pasta recipe
recipes.description: Turn flavourful sardines into a delicious sardine butter that gets tossed through this easy sardine pasta recipe.
ingredients: 75g unsalted butter, chopped, at room temperature
1 lemon, rind finely grated, lemon halved crossways
4 large vine-ripened tomatoes, deseeded, coarsely chopped
instructions: Place sardines, butter and half the semi-dried tomatoes in a food processor. Pick the leaves from half the basil and add to the food processor. Add the capers, lemon rind and then squeeze in the juice from 1 lemon half. Process until well combined, scraping down the side of the bowl with a spatula if needed until a smooth paste forms. Spoon sardine butter onto a piece of plastic wrap to form a 12cm log. Roll up wrap tightly to enclose the butter, twisting the ends to seal. Place in the fridge for 30 minutes or until firm.
Place chopped tomato and remaining semi-dried tomatoes in a large bowl. Add garlic and half of the oil, and mix to combine. Season and set aside.
Cook pasta in a large saucepan of salted, boiling water following packet directions or until al dente. Drain well, reserving 1 cup pasta water.

Meanwhile, heat remaining oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes or until browned. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel and set aside. Pick remaining basil leaves.

Wipe frying pan clean and heat over medium-high heat. Add pasta, half the sardine butter and half the reserved pasta water to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes or until the butter has melted and everything is well combined. Add the remaining sardine butter and pasta water, and cook, stirring regularly, for 1-2 minutes or until the pasta sauce has emulsified. Add the tomato mixture and basil leaves to the pan. Mix to combine, then season and serve sprinkled with toasted breadcrumbs.

recipes.title: Classic Victoria sandwich recipe
recipes.description: The perfect party cake, a Victoria sponge is a traditional bake everyone will love. Makes an easy wedding cake, too
ingredients: half a 340g jar good-quality strawberry jam
instructions: Heat oven to 190C/fan 170C/gas 5. Butter two 20cm sandwich tins and line with non-stick baking paper.
In a large bowl, beat 200g caster sugar, 200g softened butter, 4 beaten eggs, 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 2 tbsp milk together until you have a smooth, soft batter.
Divide the mixture between the tins, smooth the surface with a spatula or the back of a spoon.
Bake for about 20 mins until golden and the cake springs back when pressed.
Turn onto a cooling rack and leave to cool completely.
To make the filling, beat the 100g softened butter until smooth and creamy, then gradually beat in 140g sifted icing sugar and a drop of vanilla extract (if you’re using it).
Spread the buttercream over the bottom of one of the sponges. Top it with 170g strawberry jam and sandwich the second sponge on top.
Dust with a little icing sugar before serving. Keep in an airtight container and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: 1 Tray Creamy Chicken Fajita Pasta
recipes.description: A viral recipe that takes minimal effort as the oven does the hard work. It is tasty, packed with stellar macros, and perfect for meal prep or a family dinner with almost zero cleanup.
ingredients: Low fat cream cheese — 200g (approx. 7 oz / nearly 1 cup)
Tin (400g) chopped tomatoes — 1 tin (plus 100ml water to rinse out the tin)
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice up your chicken, onion, and peppers.
Add all of your ingredients apart from the mozzarella into a large ovenproof dish. Rinse out the tin of chopped tomatoes with 100ml of water and pour it in. Mix thoroughly.
Top with the 80g of mozzarella, cover with tin foil, and bake in the oven for 50 mins at 190°C (45 mins covered and the last 5 uncovered).
Leave to rest for 5–10 mins after cooking so all the liquid is absorbed.
Serve & enjoy!
